desc:
A land map uses 1 for a farmland cell and 0 for forest. Every maximal group of farmland cells connected through the four directions is guaranteed to fill an axis-aligned rectangle completely, and no two different groups touch each other horizontally or vertically (they may touch diagonally).

For every group return its bounding box as [r1, c1, r2, c2], where (r1, c1) is the top-left cell and (r2, c2) the bottom-right cell. Return the boxes sorted by r1, then by c1. If there is no farmland return an empty array.

land = [[1,1,0,0],
        [1,1,0,1],
        [0,0,0,1],
        [1,0,0,0]]

result = [[0,0,1,1],[1,3,2,3],[3,0,3,0]]
constraints: Every group of farmland cells is a filled rectangle; groups are never horizontally or vertically adjacent
hints: You are promised that each group is a full rectangle, so you do not need a general flood fill: the top-left corner and the bottom-right corner describe the whole group.
A cell is the top-left corner of its rectangle exactly when it is farmland and the cell above and the cell to the left are not farmland.
Scan the grid in row-major order (this also gives the required sorting). At a top-left corner, walk right while cells are farmland to find c2, and walk down to find r2.
editorial: Because every group is a filled rectangle, we can find a group by its top-left corner: a farmland cell whose upper neighbour and left neighbour are both missing or forest. No other cell of a rectangle has this property. Scanning rows from top to bottom and columns from left to right meets the corners in exactly the order the answer requires.

At each corner, extend downwards along the same column while cells are farmland to get r2, and extend to the right along the same row to get c2. The extensions cost at most the perimeter of each rectangle, so the total time is O(R · C). A flood fill that tracks the minimum and maximum row and column of each group is a more general alternative that does not depend on the rectangle guarantee.
